meta.title: Herdr SDLC Workflow
meta.subtitle: Plan, implement, verify, review, deliver, and the Herdr runtime that executes each phase.

views.label: Engineering phases
views.note: Plan the contract, implement isolated slices, verify the integrated result, review evidence, then deliver.

views.label: Herdr underneath
views.note: Graph, identity, ownership, receipt and promotion integrity are scripted; correctness checks remain explicit.

views.label: Failure and rework
views.note: Failed checks or findings return to implementation, followed by verification and review.

cards.title: Plan: make the engineering contract explicit
items: Controller investigates the target repository and defines scope, acceptance criteria, non-goals, interfaces and runnable verification before dispatch.
init-docs.py binds canonical session/run paths under the target docs root. docs/sessions/ and docs/runs/ must be Git-ignored.
accept_graph(run, graph, repo, holder) pins repo, immutable base_sha and refs/heads/herdr/<run-id>; validates nodes, aliases, dependencies, cycles and concurrent path ownership.
depends_on controls ordering; inputs declares exact consumed outputs. Ordering alone neither transfers code nor records artifact consumption.
Represent verification/review responsibilities explicitly in prompts and graph dependencies. There is no mandatory hardcoded PLAN/IMPLEMENT/VERIFY/REVIEW pipeline.
Source: scripts/init-docs.py:57-101; scripts/run_state.py:301-402,659-717.

cards.title: Implement: controller dispatches, writers own slices
items: Reconcile computes ready only after dependencies succeeded and required inputs exist. The active controller supplies exact workspace/pane/session holder and current epoch.
dispatch-agent.py records dispatch_intent once, snapshots consumed hashes and owns, then invokes spawn-agent.py --resume under dispatch_guard.

Independent writers use disjoint owned paths and separate worktrees based on the accepted base SHA. Shared files require dependency ordering; dependencies do not automatically populate worker worktrees.
New managed workers receive immutable fo- worker_id identities. launch-intent, dispatch-identity, prompt-attempt and launch-complete sidecars preserve crash evidence.
Prompt metadata includes canonical attempt_dir plus consumed artifact paths/hashes; engineering instructions, tests and review requirements remain controller-authored.
Delivery waits for observed working state. A composer stall gets one sanctioned Enter and another observation; an unstarted worker is blocked, not silently successful.
Source: scripts/dispatch-agent.py:154-225; scripts/run_state.py:1078-1122; scripts/herdr_cli.py:113-144.

cards.title: Verify: prove behavior, not merely worker settlement
items: Writers exercise their changed path and relevant regressions, report commands/results and commit before normal completion. The controller evaluates evidence against acceptance criteria.
monitor-agents.py runs as a background observer with a harness completion wakeup and/or --notify-pane. Herdr idle/done/blocked is observation, never authoritative success.
finish-agent.py requires the active holder and current attempt, clean worktree, HEAD ancestry and owned changes; publishes declared hashed attempt-local summary/VCS artifacts.
A declared worktree with no new commit is refused unless --force deliberately records the empty result. Force replacements are audited, not a rewrite of terminal success history.
The integrator explicitly applies producer changes in a separate worktree, resolves conflicts and runs verification on the combined result. No script performs the merge/cherry-pick for it.
The scripts do not run tests or score acceptance evidence. Tests and runtime checks must actually be executed by the assigned agents/controller.
Source: scripts/finish-agent.py:199-314; scripts/monitor-agents.py:160-198.

cards.title: Review: a real engineering gate, not a receipt check
items: Use a read-only reviewer to inspect the resulting implementation, requirement coverage, risks, edge cases and the observed verification evidence.
A useful review verdict distinguishes actionable findings from approval and identifies affected paths and required corrections. The controller decides whether the acceptance contract is satisfied.
Findings return to implementation, followed by renewed verification and review. A graph node's succeeded state is not a built-in semantic review approval.

Scheduling matters: a depends_on edge waits for producer succeeded, and an integrator becomes succeeded only after promotion. Pre-promotion review must be arranged explicitly while integration is held, rather than pretending an ordinary dependency provides it.

The controller can run bounded pre-promotion review against the integrator worktree/commit, then finish/promote only after the verdict is accepted; a graph-tracked post-promotion review can instead gate final branch delivery.
Receipt hashes establish lineage and integrity. Integration consumed hashes do not prove producer changes are present or correct in the final HEAD.

cards.title: Deliver: promotion is separate from human-facing publication
items: Writer/read-only finish records succeeded after declared artifact gates. Integrator finish writes integration receipts and prints the exact run_state.promote(...) call without recording succeeded.

promote validates integration/VCS receipts and exact holder/repo, refuses a checked-out promotion ref, records promotion_intent, CAS-updates only refs/heads/herdr/<run-id>, then records promoted and succeeded.

Final branch delivery requires every accepted node succeeded or skipped plus a promoted-and-succeeded integration commit. Default is feature/<slug of job>; creation is create-only and an existing different SHA is refused.
Promotion may automatically attempt final branch publication; publication failure does not undo completed promotion. deliver_branch(...) is the explicit terminal publication API.
Report the delivered SHA/branch and exercised acceptance evidence. Pushing, PR creation, merge to main, release and deployment are outside the skill.
Source: scripts/run_state.py:2338-2455.

cards.title: Authority, routing and recovery across every phase
items: events.jsonl is execution authority. state.json, controller.json and status.md are derived caches; progress/HANDOFF/NEXT are orientation and handoff notes, not success markers.
Native task/workflow executors are bounded and session-local; herdr-agent workers survive controller rotation; pane executors address existing user-owned surfaces and are never retired.
A live blocked worker may resume the same attempt after exact identity/token verification. The controller appends the returned attempt_started descriptor; do not create a second launch intent.
Failed/interrupted/invalidated retries use a new authorized attempt and immutable attempt directory. Native failed/interrupted retry additionally requires side_effect_safe=true.

Rotation is controller-triggered: rotate.py first verifies fresh same-process OMP current tokens/contextWindow >=0.5, otherwise refuses exit3 before drain/reconcile/spawn; then drain/quiescence and nonce ack, ack-handoff.py transfers the lease and increments epoch, then exact live Herdr identities are reattached.
Retire only orchestrator-owned terminal surfaces after matching identity and downstream integration receipts. Never close user panes, stop the server or discard worktrees on promotion failure.
Source: scripts/run_state.py:1754-1785,2546-2555; scripts/rotate.py; scripts/ack-handoff.py; scripts/retire-agents.py.
